note: [agent-bulk] shw 63025 (325.3 MeV, pdg 11) is the only in-scope shower and the highest-kine_charge pdg-11 object (correction 17); no higher-energy non-EM object was passed over. It has 4 members: 63025 (4.6 cm, pdg 11), 63024 (9.0 cm, pdg 11), 15003 (4.2 cm, pdg 11) and 15013 (108.5 cm, pdg 13) -- 108.5 of the shower's 126.2 cm of skeleton, 86%, is ONE straight track. 15013 is a piece of a through-going MIP: it touches the grey/unowned 15004 (63.4 cm, pdg 13) at gap 0.0 cm with only 1.5deg between their end-to-end directions, and 15004 touches the grey 15005 (131.4 cm, pdg 13) at gap 0.0 cm at 0.7deg -- 15013+15004+15005 are one 303 cm line, all in cluster 15, each with chord/pathlen 0.96-0.98 (103.8/108.5, 62.0/63.4, 129.3/131.4), i.e. straight, and each with the tight ~1 cm point spray of a MIP. You can see the join directly: in shw63025-az+085-el+20 the yellow halo stops mid-line and the identical grey line continues off the frame in the same direction; in az-055 the grey continuation runs in on the other side. The reconstruction gave the middle piece to the shower via pass4_angle at 16.0 cm / 10.5deg and left its own two neighbours grey. MARK: 15013 OUT of 63025 -- this is the strong mark, a 108.5 cm pdg-13 straight track, and the one the verdict rests on. A weaker second candidate I did NOT mark: 15003 (4.2 cm, pdg 11) came in on the same pass at the same 16.0 cm / 10.5deg and touches 15013 at gap 0.0, but at 41.4deg to it; it may be a genuine EM fragment at the junction, so I left it in -- that is the one to reverse either way. What survives the mark is 63025+63024, a compact 13.6 cm object sitting 12.0 cm from 15013 at 9.0deg; I make no claim about its energy split, only that the length is 13.6 cm of 126.2. Membership triple-check (correction 16) passes: nseg 4, owner-grouped count 4, cmp_div 4 segments -- 15013 is genuinely and solely 63025's, not a correction-11 shared segment. Vertex judged off the vtxz-* close-in sweep at 60 cm half-span (r95 = 158.1 cm, so vtxz-* fired automatically -- correction 20): the star sits at the endpoint of the grey 156.3 cm pdg-13 track 21017 with nothing else converging within 60 cm, which is a thin vertex, but the defect above is measured from the shower start and stands whatever the vertex is doing (correction 14), so this is recorded as a clustering verdict and not vertex-bad. Showers NOT looked at: the 9 skipped by the scope rule (19015 9.7, 72026 4.7, 61019 4.3, 62020 3.9, 20016 2.7, 76030 1.9, 75029 1.6, 60018 1.2, 73027 0.8 MeV), all single-segment. No reco pi0 group (all pio_id = -1); the kine_pio_* block (mass 61.6 with E1 = 9.7 MeV) is the BDT feature scan, not a pairing, and no pi0 is proposed. GATE PAIR, not an inversion but worth the owner's eye: the rejected 15004 sits at 14.9 cm / 26.1deg and the accepted 15013 at 16.0 cm / 10.5deg -- the gate did the geometrically sensible thing (accept the smaller angle at nearly the same distance) and got the physics exactly backwards, because 15004 and 15013 are the same track.
